controls.name: BPM SOURCE

controls.name: SPACING
controls.doc: Proposed dialog: beat spacing, anchored at trim start. A beat is a quarter note.

controls.name: BOUNDARY
controls.doc: Proposed dialog: exact grid or a stereo-aware quiet-boundary search within 2 ms. This does not guarantee click-free playback.

limitations: Development draft, not listed or installable.
No native slice-editor event/adapter, stock persistence integration or USB package exists yet.
No audio playback or MKII hardware verification; click-free playback is not established.
Planner accepts BPM 30–300 in 1/24 BPM units, signed 24-bit mono/stereo decoded PCM, 8–192 kHz, at most 64 slice starts.
Sample/project identity, live preview invalidation, sample-file saving and Undo must be implemented by the adapter.

tests.summary: 18 original/independent host tests, 164 compiled synchronous planner vectors, six isolated editor CPU probes, five synthetic-IO storage groups and five synthetic pool/converter groups pass. Resumable preview adds 500 host and 100 target comparisons plus lifecycle checks. No native reader, full editor, USB, audio or physical persistence qualification. Bounded PCM staging adds 4,160 decoder vectors, 40 paged previews and lifecycle tests on host/target, plus 256 exact-buffer sanitizer cases; live source access remains unimplemented. Five stock coherence groups now cover repeated PCM edits without counter changes, release/map lifetime and eight stock-page-to-host-reader previews. Native writer tracking is absent. Expanded writer probes cover eight edit families: dirty stores precede PCM, busy/counter fields stay unchanged and unmasked instruction intervals occur between PCM writes. Cross-slot copy/mix destination isolation, failed silent normalization and additional refusals are tested in synthetic memory; operation-lifetime exclusion is not implemented. Seven worker-lifecycle groups exercise a producer, real queue operations, seven edit dispatch paths and deferred completion posting. Empty queues can coexist with active edits; null callbacks or exhausted completion records omit UI notification. Synthetic FIFO and forced message reuse are covered; live scheduling, UI consumption and complete caller coverage remain unproved. A disabled-by-default portable preview admission guard adds writer tickets, global revision invalidation, nested-writer exclusion and terminal exhaustion refusal. Host and compiled-target tests cover 120 event schedules and three reader invalidation timings. The expanded stock trace covers copy/crop/release dispatch and a host guard; actual native hooks, locks and writer coverage remain absent. Three recorder groups (20 synthetic calls) cover 16/24-bit stereo page crossings, both state banks, tracks 1/8, lazy shared allocation and four early-exit/shortage paths. Position/map updates precede PCM without dirty/counter stores; allocation shortage queues follow-up work. No ISR, scheduler, remaining recorder modes or live provider is qualified. A portable serialized preview session now captures complete metadata/record snapshots, validates around bounded copies and before result publication, and handles pending/cancel/restart. Host and compiled ColdFire selftests cover 32 full previews, 22 invalidation cases and failure paths. Fourteen stock Flex load-refusal fixtures cover real release/allocation with explicit filesystem/header mocks; failed replacement can already destroy old PCM and relocate surviving maps. Native callbacks, writer coverage and live admission are still absent. Pure marker candidate preparation now preserves complete existing records and ordinals, retains all inactive rows in before/after snapshots, and refuses missing/renumbered/overlapping/short or unsupported records without output mutation. Host and compiled ColdFire tests cover 2,144 retained-prefix candidates and 386 full-table stale comparisons. Twenty-four synthetic Flex/Static candidates remain exact through stock sort/sanitation with explicit follow-up mocks. Native atomic Apply/Undo and playback qualification remain absent. Five stock-pool session groups connect host session callbacks to real Flex page lookup, gain and release: eight complete previews, four PCM-writer invalidations, three result-metadata invalidations, released-source refusal and pending/copy-time mutation handling pass. Identity, lock, rate and tempo are synthetic; no native provider or device is qualified. Four stock editor-publication groups execute 24 immediate grids, four deferred grids, four busy-source refusals and redraw-only behavior. Grid creation clears count before deferred zero searches and writes records unmasked before pointer/selection refresh. Display/progress/zero searches are mocks; no atomic Apply, Undo or physical persistence is qualified. Preview-bound edit candidates now receive unique operation IDs, bind to the exact ready session, capture all 64 records under supplied ownership and revalidate source plus full before-table before returning a candidate. Host and compiled ColdFire tests pass 40 candidates, 193 full-table mutations, 21 metadata changes and pending/cancel/restart/refusal cases; the existing 32-preview/22-invalidation session suite still passes. No native Apply/Undo is enabled. A native Flex copy component validates readiness, format/length, descriptor geometry, current map pointer ranges, allocation extent and physical page before invoking a reviewed stock lookup through an original ColdFire D0/D1 ABI shim. Host sanitizers and actual compiled-target/stock execution pass 96 copies, 34 precondition refusals, four malformed replies, short capacity and four relocated-map cases. No lock, writer coverage, live binding or source admission is installed. The complete planner/decoder/session/candidate chain now executes as compiled ColdFire code against real stock Flex lookup and gain, with a synthetic provider/lock/identity/rate/tempo fixture. Thirty-two full chains preserve PCM/settings and match reference plans; four metadata/inactive-record/actual-gain stale cases refuse results, including partial-preview invalidation. The raw-copy regression suite is included. This remains a test provider, not live source admission or an installable module.

access.location: Proposed MKII audio editor SLICE menu; unavailable in firmware
steps: Pending native integration: select a Flex or Static audio track and open AED.
Proposed: press LFO for SLICE, FUNC + YES for its menu, then select BEAT GRID. Stock menu integration is not verified.
Choose BPM SOURCE, SPACING and BOUNDARY, preview the marker count and warnings, then explicitly Apply or Cancel. Do not use this proposal as instructions for an existing build.
